subject: maths
title: Angles and Shapes: Acute and Obtuse Angles, Triangles and Quadrilaterals
seo_title: Year 4 Angles and Shapes Worksheets: Acute and Obtuse Angles, Triangles, Quadrilaterals (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Compare and classify geometric shapes, including quadrilaterals and triangles, based on their properties and sizes; identify acute and obtuse angles and compare and order angles up to two right angles by size.
meta_desc: Free Year 4 maths worksheets on angles and shapes: acute, right and obtuse angles, comparing and ordering angles, equilateral, isosceles, scalene and right-angled triangles, and quadrilaterals such as the trapezium, rhombus and kite. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: Compare every angle with a right angle: smaller is acute, bigger is obtuse, and two right angles make a straight line.
key_sub: The size of an angle is how wide it opens, not how long its arms are. Sort triangles and quadrilaterals by their equal sides, parallel sides and right angles; turning a shape never changes its name.
body_html:
Acute, right angle or obtuse?

An angle shows how far something turns. Compare every angle with a right angle: a square corner, like the corner of a page. A small square in a corner shows a right angle.

AngleCompared with a right angle
AcuteSmaller than a right angle (less than 90°)
Right angleA square corner, a quarter turn (90°)
ObtuseBigger than a right angle, smaller than a straight line
Straight lineTwo right angles (180°)
Example

A clock shows 4 o’clock. What kind of angle do the hands make?

A right angle is 3 hour marks (3 o’clock). A straight line is 6 hour marks (6 o’clock). 4 hour marks is in between.

Answer: obtuse

Compare and order angles

To compare angles, look at how wide each one opens. Do not look at the length of the arms.

Example

Order these angles from smallest to largest: an obtuse angle, a right angle, an acute angle.

Acute is smaller than a right angle, and obtuse is bigger.

Answer: acute, right angle, obtuse

Triangles

Small lines on the sides, called tick marks, show sides that are the same length.

TriangleWhat it has
Equilateral3 equal sides and 3 equal angles
IsoscelesExactly 2 equal sides (and 2 equal angles)
ScaleneNo equal sides
Right-angled1 right angle

Quadrilaterals

A quadrilateral has 4 straight sides. Arrows on two sides show that they are parallel: they go the same way and never meet.

ShapeEqual sidesParallel sidesRight angles
Square4 equal sides2 pairs4
RectangleOpposite sides equal2 pairs4
Rhombus4 equal sides2 pairsNone (unless it is a square)
ParallelogramOpposite sides equal2 pairsNone (unless it is a rectangle)
TrapeziumCan varyExactly 1 pairCan have 2
Kite2 pairs next to each otherNoneUsually none
Example

I have 4 equal sides and no right angles. What shape am I?

4 equal sides could be a square or a rhombus. A square has 4 right angles, so it is not a square.

Answer: a rhombus

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Thinking longer arms make a bigger angleLook at how wide the angle opens
Saying a turned square is not a squareTurning does not change a shape. Check the sides and angles
Calling every 4-sided shape a rectangleA rectangle must have 4 right angles
Mixing up isosceles and equilateralIsosceles: exactly 2 equal sides. Equilateral: all 3 equal
Calling an angle bigger than a straight line obtuseObtuse angles are smaller than a straight line (two right angles)

faq.q: What do Year 4 children learn about angles?
faq.a: They learn to spot acute and obtuse angles by comparing them with a right angle, and to compare and order angles up to two right angles (a straight line).

faq.q: Do Year 4 pupils measure angles with a protractor?
faq.a: No. In Year 4 they compare angles with a right angle. Measuring angles in degrees with a protractor starts in Year 5.

faq.q: What is the difference between an isosceles and an equilateral triangle?
faq.a: An isosceles triangle has exactly 2 equal sides. An equilateral triangle has all 3 sides equal and all 3 angles equal.
A trapezium is a quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides. In the US the same shape is called a trapezoid.

items.q: What is an acute angle?
items.e: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle (less than 90°).

items.q: A right angle is a quarter turn. How many degrees is a right angle?
items.e: A right angle is 90°. A straight line (two right angles) is 180°.

items.q: What kind of angle is this?
items.e: The angle is smaller than a right angle (a square corner), so it is acute.

items.q: Which angle is acute?

items.q: What kind of angle is this?
items.e: The angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line, so it is obtuse.
The two arms point in opposite directions and make a straight line. That is two right angles (180°).

items.q: What is an obtuse angle?
c: between a right angle and a straight line
items.e: An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle (90°) but smaller than a straight line (180°).

Yes, short arms make it acute

items.q: How many right angles make a straight line?
items.e: A right angle is 90° and a straight line is 180°. 90° + 90° = 180°, so 2 right angles make a straight line.

items.q: Charlie draws an angle that is bigger than one right angle but smaller than two right angles. What kind of angle is it?
items.e: Two right angles make a straight line. An angle between one right angle and a straight line is obtuse.

items.e: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle, and an obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle.

items.q: Which two angles in this trapezium are obtuse?
items.e: The two top angles, C and D, open wider than a right angle. The two bottom angles, A and B, are acute.

c: No, P is a right angle
No, P is larger: its arms are longer
Yes, they open the same amount
items.e: Both angles open by the same amount. P only has longer arms, and arm length does not change the size of an angle.

items.q: Which angle in this kite is the smallest?
items.e: Angle C is the only acute angle: it is the sharpest point of the kite. Angles A, B and D are obtuse.

items.q: Which angle is larger?
items.e: Angle Q is obtuse and angle P is acute, so Q is larger. P has longer arms, but that does not make the angle bigger.

items.q: Which angle is the largest?

items.q: How many obtuse angles does this shape have?
items.e: All 6 angles of this hexagon are bigger than a right angle, so all 6 are obtuse.

items.q: Which is larger: an obtuse angle or a right angle?
items.e: An obtuse angle is always bigger than a right angle. That is what obtuse means.

items.q: Which angle is the largest?
items.e: Picture D opens the widest. The other obtuse angle is only a little bigger than a right angle.

sets.title: Equilateral, isosceles, scalene and right-angled triangles

items.q: What type of triangle is this? Look at the marks on the sides.
items.e: The tick marks show exactly 2 equal sides, so it is an isosceles triangle.

items.q: A triangle has sides of 6 cm, 7 cm and 9 cm. What type of triangle is it?
items.e: All 3 sides are different lengths, so it is scalene.

items.q: What type of triangle is this? Look at the marks on the sides.
items.e: Count the sides: there are 4, because the top corner is cut off. A triangle has exactly 3 sides.

items.q: What type of triangle is this? Look at the marks on the sides.
items.e: The tick marks show that all 3 sides are equal, so it is an equilateral triangle. Turning a triangle does not change its type.

items.q: How many equal sides does an isosceles triangle have?
items.e: An isosceles triangle has exactly 2 equal sides. A triangle with 3 equal sides is equilateral.

items.q: A triangle has sides of 5 cm, 5 cm and 8 cm. What type of triangle is it?
items.e: Two sides are 5 cm, so exactly 2 sides are equal. That makes it isosceles. It is not equilateral, because 8 cm is different.

items.q: Which is a right-angled triangle?
items.e: Picture D has a right angle (the small square). The others have no right angle.

items.q: What type of triangle is this? Look at the marks on the sides.
items.e: There are no tick marks: all 3 sides are different lengths, so it is a scalene triangle.

items.q: Which triangle is scalene?
items.e: Picture B has no tick marks: all 3 sides are different lengths. The others have at least 2 equal sides.

items.q: What type of triangle is this? Look at the marks on the sides.
items.e: The tick marks show exactly 2 equal sides, so it is an isosceles triangle. Turning a triangle does not change its type.

items.q: Evie says this triangle is equilateral. Is she right?
items.e: Only the 2 long sides have tick marks, so exactly 2 sides are equal. It is isosceles, not equilateral.

items.q: Which triangle is isosceles?
items.e: Picture A has exactly 2 sides with tick marks. The others have no equal sides: they are scalene.

items.q: Which names fit this triangle?
items.e: The small square shows a right angle, and the tick marks show 2 equal sides. So it is right-angled and isosceles.

items.q: This triangle has a right angle. Which names fit it?
items.e: The small square shows a right angle, so it is right-angled. No sides are marked equal, so it is also scalene.

items.q: Can a triangle have 2 right angles?
c: No, the sides would not meet
Yes, if it is very big
items.e: If 2 angles were right angles, the 2 sides going up from them would be parallel and never meet. The shape could not close.

items.q: What type of triangle is this? Look at the marks on the sides.
items.e: There are no tick marks: all 3 sides are different lengths, so it is a scalene triangle. Turning a triangle does not change its type.

items.q: What type of triangle is this? Look at the marks on the sides.
items.e: The tick marks show that all 3 sides are equal, so it is an equilateral triangle.

items.q: Which triangle is equilateral?
items.e: Picture C has the same tick mark on all 3 sides. The two isosceles triangles have only 2 equal sides, and the scalene one has none.

items.q: What is true about the angles of an equilateral triangle?
items.e: An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides and 3 equal angles. Each angle is acute (60°).

items.q: What type of triangle is this? Look at the marks on the sides.
items.e: The tick marks show exactly 2 equal sides, so it is an isosceles triangle.

sets.title: Quadrilaterals: square, rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram, trapezium and kite

items.q: Which shape has exactly one pair of parallel sides?
items.e: Picture D is a trapezium: only its top and bottom are parallel. The parallelogram and rectangle have 2 pairs, and the kite has none.

items.q: Leo says every shape with 4 sides is a rectangle. Is he right?
c: No, a rectangle needs 4 right angles
items.e: This shape has 4 sides but no right angles, so it is not a rectangle. It is a trapezium: only 1 pair of sides is parallel.

items.q: What do the arrows on the top and bottom sides show?
items.e: Matching arrows show parallel sides: they go in the same direction and never meet.

items.q: The arrows show parallel sides. Which shape is NOT a parallelogram?
items.e: Picture B has only 1 pair of parallel sides, so it is a trapezium. A parallelogram has 2 pairs. Rectangles and rhombuses have 2 pairs of parallel sides, so they are special parallelograms.

items.q: Which shape has 4 equal sides but no right angles?
items.e: Picture C is a rhombus: all 4 sides have the same tick mark and there are no small squares. The square has right angles, and the kite and rectangle do not have 4 equal sides.

items.q: What is the name of this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 2 pairs of equal sides that are next to each other, not opposite. It has no parallel sides, so it is a kite.

items.q: Is a square also a rectangle?
c: No, its sides are all equal
items.e: A rectangle is a 4-sided shape with 4 right angles. A square has 4 right angles too, so it is a special rectangle with 4 equal sides.

items.q: What is the name of this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides, and there are no right angles, so it is a rhombus.

items.q: What is the name of this quadrilateral?
items.e: The arrows show exactly 1 pair of parallel sides, so it is a trapezium. The right angles do not make it a rectangle: a rectangle has 4.

items.q: What is the name of this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 2 pairs of equal sides that are next to each other, not opposite. It has no parallel sides, so it is a kite.

items.q: What is the name of this quadrilateral?
items.e: The tick marks show 4 equal sides and the small squares show 4 right angles, so it is a square. Standing on a corner does not change it: it is still a square.

items.q: Maya sorts shapes into “has a right angle” and “no right angle”. Which shape goes in “no right angle”?
items.e: A rhombus that is not a square has no right angles. A square and a rectangle have 4, and a right-angled triangle has 1.

items.q: What do the small lines (tick marks) on the sides show?
items.e: Sides with the same tick marks are the same length. One tick shows one pair, two ticks show another pair.

items.q: Which shape has 2 pairs of equal sides that are next to each other, and no parallel sides?
items.e: A kite has 2 pairs of equal sides next to each other. A parallelogram and a rectangle have equal sides opposite each other.

items.q: A shape has 2 pairs of parallel sides. Its opposite sides are equal, but not all 4 sides are equal, and it has no right angles. What is it?
items.e: 2 pairs of parallel sides make a parallelogram. With no right angles it is not a rectangle, and without 4 equal sides it is not a rhombus.

items.q: What is the name of this quadrilateral?
items.e: The small squares show 4 right angles, and only the opposite sides are equal, so it is a rectangle.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does a parallelogram have?
items.e: The opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel: top and bottom, left and right. That is 2 pairs (4 is the number of sides).

items.q: What is the name of this quadrilateral?
items.e: The arrows show exactly 1 pair of parallel sides, so it is a trapezium.

items.q: What is the name of this quadrilateral?
items.e: The arrows show 2 pairs of parallel sides. There are no right angles and the sides are not all equal, so it is a parallelogram.

items.q: Which shape has 4 right angles but NOT 4 equal sides?
items.e: Picture A is a rectangle. The turned square has 4 right angles too, but its 4 sides are equal. The rhombus has no right angles, and the trapezium has only 2.

sets.title: Clocks, road signs, letters and shape riddles

items.q: I have 4 equal sides and no right angles. What shape am I?
items.e: 4 equal sides with no right angles make a rhombus. A square has 4 equal sides too, but it has 4 right angles.

items.q: How many right angles are inside the capital letter T?
items.e: Where the top line meets the stem, there is a right angle on each side. That is 2 right angles.

items.q: What kind of angle do the hands make?
items.e: At 3 o’clock the hands make a square corner: a quarter turn, 90°.

items.q: Which capital letter has an obtuse angle?
items.e: Where the two lines of X cross, two of the angles are obtuse (and two are acute). L, E and F only have right angles.

items.q: A warning road sign is a triangle with 3 equal sides. What type of triangle is it?
items.e: 3 equal sides make an equilateral triangle. Its 3 angles are equal too.

items.q: What kind of angle do the hands make?
items.e: At 4 o’clock the hands are 4 hour marks apart. A right angle is 3 hour marks, and a straight line is 6, so the angle is obtuse.

items.q: I am a triangle. Exactly 2 of my sides are equal. What am I?
items.e: A triangle with exactly 2 equal sides is isosceles. Equilateral would need 3 equal sides.

items.q: A clock shows 2 o’clock. What kind of angle do the hour hand and the minute hand make?
items.e: At 2 o’clock the hands are 2 hour marks apart. A right angle is 3 hour marks, so the angle is smaller: it is acute.

items.q: What kind of angle do the hands make?
items.e: At 10 o’clock the hands are 2 hour marks apart. That is less than a quarter turn (3 hour marks), so the angle is acute.

items.q: At which time do the hands of a clock make a right angle?
items.e: At 9 o’clock the hands point to 12 and 9: a quarter turn apart, which is a right angle.

items.q: I have 4 right angles and 4 equal sides. What shape am I?
items.e: 4 right angles and 4 equal sides make a square. A rectangle has 4 right angles, but not always 4 equal sides.

items.q: At which time do the hands of a clock make a straight line?
items.e: At 6 o’clock the hands point to 12 and 6, in opposite directions, so they make a straight line. At 3 and 9 o’clock they make right angles, and at 12 o’clock they are on top of each other.

items.q: A clock shows 8 o’clock. What kind of angle is the smaller angle between the hands?
items.e: From 8 to 12 is 4 hour marks. That is more than a right angle (3 hour marks) but less than a straight line (6), so it is obtuse.

items.q: Poppy folds a square piece of paper in half from one corner to the opposite corner. What type of triangle does she make?
items.e: The triangle keeps one corner of the square, which is a right angle. Its two short sides are sides of the square, so they are equal: it is right-angled and isosceles.

items.q: Which capital letter has an acute angle?
items.e: V has an acute angle at the bottom point. L, T and H only have right angles.

items.q: I have 4 sides and exactly one pair of parallel sides. What shape am I?
items.e: Exactly 1 pair of parallel sides makes a trapezium. A parallelogram and a rectangle have 2 pairs, and a kite has none.

items.q: Amelia opens a door a little way, less than a right angle from the wall. What kind of angle do the door and the wall make?
items.e: The door has turned less than a right angle, so the angle is acute.

items.q: What kind of angle do the hands make?
items.e: At 6 o’clock one hand points to 12 and the other to 6. Together they make a straight line: two right angles.

items.q: A give way sign is the same triangle turned upside down. Alfie says it is not equilateral any more. Is he right?
items.e: Turning a shape does not change its sides or angles. The 3 sides are still equal, so it is still equilateral.

items.q: How many right angles are inside the capital letter E?
items.e: There is 1 right angle at the top corner, 1 at the bottom corner and 2 where the middle line meets the upright: 4 in all.
